top_story.headline: A discharge petition on immigration status sits one signature short of 218
top_story.dek: Both chambers met only briefly in pro forma sessions on Thursday, so the petition tally is the most consequential item this week.
paragraphs: Discharge Petition No. 25, which would force consideration of H.R. 1589 (a bill to authorize the cancellation of removal and adjustment of status of certain aliens), stands at 217 of 218 signatures, one short of the number needed. It was filed through H.Res. 1414, sponsored by Rep. Sylvia R. Garcia. No open petition gained signatures between October 27 and today.

Discharge Petition No. 27, sponsored by Rep. Thomas Massie for H.R. 185, has 216 of 218 signatures. Discharge Petition No. 3 (H.R. 185, sponsored by Rep. Brendan F. Boyle) and Discharge Petition No. 24 (H.R. 7007, sponsored by Rep. Jamie Raskin) each have 212.

The floor itself was quiet. The Senate met for under a minute in a pro forma session, and the House met for about two minutes with no recorded votes. Both chambers next meet in pro forma sessions on Monday, November 2.

sections.headline: Pro forma sessions in both chambers, 13 committee reports and 34 new House bills
paragraphs: The Senate met at 2:00:01 p.m. in a pro forma session and adjourned at 2:00:39 p.m. until 4:30 p.m. on Monday, November 2. No Senate committee meetings were held.

The House met at 12 noon and adjourned at 12:02 p.m., with no Yea and Nay votes, no recorded votes and no quorum calls. No House hearings were held. Representative Smith of New Jersey served as Speaker pro tempore. The House introduced 34 public bills (H.R. 10918-10951), one concurrent resolution and four resolutions, and filed 13 committee reports, most from the House Committee on Natural Resources. The House will next meet in a pro forma session at 2 p.m. on Monday, November 2.

The introduced measures are mostly routine. The ones likeliest to draw attention are Rep. DeLauro's Medicare for America health program bill, Rep. Casar's resolution against federal bailouts of companies exposed to the artificial intelligence market, and Rep. Moore's bill to bar lobbying for the Nigerian government.

items: H.R. 3331, reported by committee (House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure, H. Rept. 119-853, with an amendment), sponsored by Rep. Salud Carbajal (D-CA-24) — the Mariner Exam Modernization Act, on merchant mariner credential examination working groups.

H.R. 4598, reported by committee (House Committee on Natural Resources, H. Rept. 119-854, with an amendment), sponsored by Rep. Teresa Leger Fernandez (D-NM-3) — technical corrections to the Navajo Nation Water Resources Development Trust Fund, the Taos Pueblo Water Development Fund and the Aamodt Settlement Pueblos' Fund.

H.R. 7254, reported by committee (House Committee on Natural Resources, H. Rept. 119-855, with an amendment), sponsored by Rep. Jared Huffman (D-CA-2) — directs the Secretary of the Interior to study the feasibility of designating the Bay Area Ridge National Scenic Trail.

H.R. 7954, reported by committee (House Committee on Natural Resources, H. Rept. 119-856), sponsored by Rep. Jeff Hurd (R-CO-3) — the Don Young Doug LaMalfa Indian Buffalo Management Act, to help Tribal governments manage buffalo and buffalo habitat and reestablish buffalo on Indian land.

H.R. 8195, reported by committee (House Committee on Natural Resources, H. Rept. 119-857, with an amendment), sponsored by Rep. Tim Walberg (R-MI-5) — the Responsible Cormorant Management and Control Act of 2026, requiring regional management frameworks for the take of double-crested cormorants.

H.R. 8483, reported by committee (House Committee on Natural Resources, H. Rept. 119-858, with an amendment), sponsored by Rep. Darrell Issa (R-CA-48) — the Barona Group of Capitan Grande Band of Mission Indians Land Transfer Act of 2026, taking certain California land into trust for the Barona Group.

H.R. 9269, reported by committee (House Committee on Natural Resources, H. Rept. 119-859, with an amendment), sponsored by Rep. James Clyburn (D-SC-6) — the Renewing the African American Civil Rights Network Act, extending that network's authorization.

H.R. 9600, reported by committee (House Committee on Natural Resources, H. Rept. 119-860), sponsored by Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-MD-8) — the Common Sense 250 Act of 2026, approving the location of a commemorative work for Thomas Paine.

H.R. 8183, reported by committee (House Committee on Education and Workforce, H. Rept. 119-861, with amendments), sponsored by Rep. Burgess Owens (R-UT-4) — the MATCH Act of 2026, amending the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act to provide for talent marketplaces.

H.R. 9640, reported by committee (House Committee on Natural Resources, H. Rept. 119-862, with an amendment), sponsored by Rep. Robert Wittman (R-VA-1) — the Earth MRI Reauthorization Act of 2026, reauthorizing the Earth Mapping Resources Initiative.

H.R. 9785, reported by committee (House Committee on Natural Resources, H. Rept. 119-863, with an amendment), sponsored by Rep. Dusty Johnson (R-SD) — the South Dakota Water Feasibility Studies Act, directing feasibility studies of municipal, rural and industrial water projects in parts of the Missouri River basin.

H.R. 10136, reported by committee (House Committee on Natural Resources, H. Rept. 119-864, with an amendment), sponsored by Rep. Bruce Westerman (R-AR-4) — the Crossett Experimental Forest Act of 2026, conveying the forest to the State of Arkansas.

H.R. 10306, reported by committee (House Committee on Natural Resources, H. Rept. 119-865, with an amendment), sponsored by Rep. Mark Amodei (R-NV-2) — a technical correction to the Shoshone-Paiute Tribes of the Duck Valley Reservation Water Rights Settlement Act of 2025.

S. 675, a Senate-passed bill reported by the House Committee on Natural Resources (H. Rept. 119-866) — contributes funds and artifacts to the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library in Medora, North Dakota. The sponsor lookup did not cover this measure.

H.R. 10918, sponsored by Rep. Jodey Arrington (R-TX-19) — bars the Environmental Protection Agency from requiring continuous monitoring of the net heating value of certain combustion control devices under the Clean Air Act; referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10919, sponsored by Rep. Jack Bergman (R-MI-1) — ensures certain safety net providers do not pay more than the 340B ceiling price for covered outpatient drugs at the time of purchase; referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10920, sponsored by Rep. Kat Cammack (R-FL-3) — reauthorizes grants to State professional licensing boards to reduce regulatory barriers to telemedicine; referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10921, sponsored by Rep. Judy Chu (D-CA-28) — provides Medicare coverage for custom fabricated breast prostheses following a mastectomy; referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce and, in addition, the House Committee on Ways and Means.

H.R. 10922, sponsored by Rep. Ben Cline (R-VA-6) — imposes liability on State officers and employees who fail to prevent fraud; referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary and four other committees.

H.R. 10923, sponsored by Rep. Steve Cohen (D-TN-9) — overhauls the Controlled Substances Act, with a new scheduling system and support for scientific research; referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce and five other committees.

H.R. 10924, sponsored by Rep. Rosa DeLauro (D-CT-3) — establishes a Medicare for America health program to provide comprehensive health coverage for all Americans; referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means and five other committees.

H.R. 10925, sponsored by Rep. James Gallagher (R-CA-1) — requires an assessment of the State Department's technical capacity to address the use of artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies to facilitate human trafficking; referred to the House Committee on Foreign Affairs.
H.R. 10926, sponsored by Rep. Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ-5) — protects election workers and polling places; referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.
H.R. 10927, sponsored by Rep. Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ-5) — amends the Voting Rights Act of 1965 to prohibit destroying or damaging ballot boxes; referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.

H.R. 10928, sponsored by Rep. Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ-5) — authorizes the Secretary of Agriculture to give States block grants for crop losses from freezes or cold weather in April 2026; referred to the House Committee on Agriculture.

H.R. 10929, sponsored by Rep. Val Hoyle (D-OR-4) — imposes a 50 percent duty on hemp products imported from China and sets mandatory testing for imports of certain cannabinoid products; referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.

H.R. 10930, sponsored by Rep. Sydney Kamlager-Dove (D-CA-37) — accounts for the age of certain juvenile offenders in federal law and funds grants for collaboration between State child welfare and juvenile justice systems; referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary and, in addition, the House Committee on Ways and Means.

H.R. 10931, sponsored by Rep. Thomas Kean (R-NJ-7) — directs the Institute of Museum and Library Services to award grants for public library construction; referred to the House Committee on Education and Workforce.

H.R. 10932, sponsored by Rep. Thomas Kean (R-NJ-7) — directs the Federal Emergency Management Agency to give requesting States and tribes its major disaster recommendation report and to develop factors for recommending a declaration for snowstorms; referred to the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure.

H.R. 10933, sponsored by Rep. Thomas Kean (R-NJ-7) — directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to make grants for emergency medical services activities; referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
H.R. 10934, sponsored by Rep. Teresa Leger Fernandez (D-NM-3) — modifies the requirements applicable to certain locatable minerals; referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources.

H.R. 10935, sponsored by Rep. Zoe Lofgren (D-CA-18) — directs the Secretary of the Interior to sell certain Bureau of Land Management land in Monterey County, California; referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources.
H.R. 10936, sponsored by Rep. Nancy Mace (R-SC-1) — deems covered color additives unsafe; referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10937, sponsored by Rep. Doris Matsui (D-CA-7) — ensures equitable treatment of covered entities and pharmacies in the 340B drug discount program; referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce and, in addition, the House Committee on Ways and Means.
H.R. 10938, sponsored by Rep. Max Miller (R-OH-7) — raises the maximum home health service benefit for certain veterans; referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.

H.R. 10939, sponsored by Rep. Barry Moore (R-AL-1) — prohibits compensated lobbying on behalf of the Nigerian government while it is designated a country of particular concern for religious freedom; referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.

H.R. 10940, sponsored by Rep. Kevin Mullin (D-CA-15) — directs the Federal Communications Commission to set metrics, goals and minimum requirements for the delivery of wireless emergency alerts; referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10941, sponsored by Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-MD-8) — amends section 5 of the Clayton Act so courts consider proposed voluntary dismissals when reviewing proposed consent judgments; referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.
H.R. 10942, sponsored by Rep. Mary Gay Scanlon (D-PA-5) — prohibits bankruptcy bonuses to highly compensated employees and insiders of the debtor; referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.

H.R. 10943, sponsored by Rep. Hillary Scholten (D-MI-3) — directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to provide counsel for unaccompanied alien children in immigration proceedings; referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.

H.R. 10944, sponsored by Rep. W. Steube (R-FL-17) — excludes from gross income certain retirement plan distributions used for a home down payment or closing costs; referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.

H.R. 10945, sponsored by Rep. Emilia Sykes (D-OH-13) — excludes from the anti-kickback statute certain remuneration for providing food or nutrition services; referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce and, in addition, the House Committee on Ways and Means.

H.R. 10946, sponsored by Rep. Mark Takano (D-CA-39) — renames the Office of Technology Assessment the Congressional Office of Technology and revises its functions and duties; referred to the House Committee on House Administration.

H.R. 10947, sponsored by Rep. Rashida Tlaib (D-MI-12) — directs the Environmental Protection Agency to add certain nanoplastics and microplastics to the Safe Drinking Water Act list of unregulated contaminants; referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10948, sponsored by Rep. Derrick Van Orden (R-WI-3) — extends the veterans' employment emphasis under Federal contracts to military spouses and raises the applicability thresholds; referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.

H.R. 10949, sponsored by Rep. Gabe Vasquez (D-NM-2) — directs the Secretary of Defense to expand the priority list for the Public Schools on Military Installations Program; referred to the House Committee on Education and Workforce.

H.R. 10950, sponsored by Rep. Eugene Vindman (D-VA-7) — requires sponsors of large data centers to file public disclosure statements with the Secretary of Energy; referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10951, sponsored by Rep. George Whitesides (D-CA-27) — amends the Commodity Exchange Act to prohibit the listing of contracts relating to wildfires; referred to the House Committee on Agriculture.

H. Con. Res. 125, sponsored by Rep. Lois Frankel (Florida) — expresses support for designating November 9 through November 15, 2026, as "National Caregiving Youth Week" for children and adolescents under 18 who serve as caregivers; referred to the House Committee on Education and Workforce.

H. Res. 1642, sponsored by Rep. Greg Casar (D-TX-35) — expresses the sense of the House that Congress must refuse additional funds or exceptional regulatory support to companies or financial institutions facing collapse from exposure to the artificial intelligence market, and must support harmed Americans instead; referred to the House Committee on Financial Services and two other committees.

H. Res. 1643, sponsored by Rep. Gilbert Cisneros (D-CA-31) — recognizes the contributions of Hispanic and Latino servicemembers and promotes Hispanic and Latino leadership across the military; referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.

H. Res. 1644, sponsored by Rep. Al Green (D-TX-9) — supports the goals and ideals of October as "National Domestic Violence Awareness Month"; referred to the House Committee on Education and Workforce.

H. Res. 1645, sponsored by Rep. Chris Pappas (D-NH-1) — supports designating October 28 as "Oxi Day" to commemorate Greek Prime Minister Ioannis Metaxas's "No!" to surrender to the Axis forces; referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
